Files an application's users upload (docs/files/design.md). It is the counterpart of the Java `egradx-file-storage`, with the same endpoints (`contracts/openapi/files.yaml`), table and history table (`contracts/db/postgresql/files`), permissions, audit actions and error codes, so Node, Java and Python applications can share one database and one bucket.

- **Files belong to an organization.** A file of another organization answers 404. Inside the caller's organization, a refusal answers 403.
- **Permissions:** `egradx.file.read`, `egradx.file.write` and `egradx.file.delete` are contributed to egradx-auth, and every organization's Admin role holds them. The uploader may always read and delete their own file.
- **Attached files:** a file attached to an application record (`attachedType`/`attachedId`) is decided by the application's `EgradxFileAccessPolicy` for that type. It answers `ALLOW`, `DENY` or `DEFAULT`, and `DEFAULT` leaves it to the permissions.
- **Profile photos:** `PUT /egradx/auth/my/profile/photo` stores one and sets the profile's `photoUrl` to `/egradx/files/{id}/content`. Everyone in the organization can read it.
- **Backends:** local disk, or any S3-compatible store through the official AWS SDK. `@aws-sdk/client-s3` and `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner` are optional peer dependencies, so local disk needs neither.
- **Downloads** are streamed after the check, with `ETag`, `Content-Disposition` (inline only for images other than SVG, and PDF) and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. A single `Range` answers 206. On S3 you can turn on a pre-signed redirect (302) instead.
- **Uploads** are read with [busboy](https://www.npmjs.com/package/busboy) into a temporary file, as Spring's multipart resolver does. Reading stops at the larger of `maxSize` and `profilePhoto.maxSize`.

```ts
import { createFileStorage, fileAccessPolicy } from '@babulvaibhav/egradx-file-storage';

// With @babulvaibhav/egradx-sdk: connected to egradx-auth, started and closed with the rest, mounted by egradxRoutes,
// and its table migrated by migrateEgradx (whenever this package is installed).
const egradx = createEgradx({ prisma, auth: { … }, files: createFileStorage({
  local: { root: './files' },
  policies: [fileAccessPolicy('order', async (request) => (await canSee(request) ? 'DEFAULT' : 'DENY'))],
}) });
```

Without the umbrella:

```ts
import { createFiles, migrateFiles } from '@babulvaibhav/egradx-file-storage';
import { fileRoutes } from '@babulvaibhav/egradx-file-storage/express';

await migrateFiles(databaseUrl);                 // egradx_file, into egradx_files_schema_history
const files = createFiles({ prisma, auth });      // before auth.start(): it contributes the permissions
app.use(fileRoutes(files));                       // after authenticateWith(auth), before the error handler
await files.start();                              // checks the backend and starts the hourly clean-up
```

## Settings (Java's `egradx.files.*`)

| Setting | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `backend` | `local` | `local` or `s3` |
| `local.root` | `./egradx-files` | |
| `s3.bucket`, `s3.region` (`us-east-1`), `s3.endpoint`, `s3.pathStyle` (false), `s3.accessKey`, `s3.secretKey` | | without keys, the AWS SDK's default credentials |
| `s3.presignedDownloads`, `s3.presignedTtlMs` | false, 5 minutes | |
| `maxSize` | `25MB` | bytes, or Spring's form: `64KB`, `25MB` |
| `allowedContentTypes` | empty (any) | e.g. `['image/*', 'application/pdf']` |
| `profilePhoto.maxSize`, `profilePhoto.contentTypes` | `5MB`, PNG/JPEG/WebP | |
| `cleanup.enabled`, `cleanup.intervalMs` | true, hourly | removes the bytes of deleted files whose removal failed |
| `store`, `s3Client`, `policies`, `scanners` | | the application's own store, S3 client, access checks and scanners (`EgradxFileScanner`: refuses with `FILE_REJECTED`, 422) |

Java's `schema.migrate` has no counterpart here: Node applications call `migrateFiles` (or `migrateEgradx`) themselves.

## Tests

- `files.test.ts` is Java's `EgradxFilesHttpTest`, on PostgreSQL (`EGRADX_TEST_PG_*`, default localhost:5432 postgres/postgres) and local disk. It also covers the contract's response schemas, the clean-up, a scanner's refusal and the `photoUrl` rule.
- `names.test.ts` covers file names, content types, `Content-Disposition` and sizes, which Java computes the same way.
- `s3.test.ts` needs `EGRADX_TEST_S3_ENDPOINT`, e.g. `http://localhost:9000`, and optionally `EGRADX_TEST_S3_ACCESS_KEY`, `_SECRET_KEY` and `_BUCKET` (default `egradx-node-test`, created if missing). It covers the store, uploads and ranges through the application, and the pre-signed redirect.

### EgradxFileException

A refusal particular to files, with the HTTP status it answers: FILE_TOO_LARGE (413), FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED (415),
FILE_EMPTY (400), FILE_REJECTED (422), FILE_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE (503). The generic cases use egradx-core's exceptions.

### EgradxFileService

Uploads, reads, lists and deletes files (docs/files/design.md). Every call names its caller, and a file outside the
caller's organization does not exist for them (404).

Who may do what: the uploader may always read and delete their own file; a profile photo is readable by anyone in its
organization and deletable only by its owner; a file attached to an application record is decided by the
EgradxFileAccessPolicy for its type, when there is one; otherwise the permissions egradx.file.read, .write and .delete
decide. As Java's EgradxFileService.

### EgradxLocalBlobStore

Files in a folder: each key is a path under `root`. A file is written to a temporary name and moved into place, so a
reader never sees half of one. With several instances, `root` must be a folder they all share. As Java's EgradxLocalBlobStore.

### EgradxFileAccessPolicy

The application's own check for files attached to one kind of its records (`attachedType`: `order`, `ticket`, …). Pass
one per type. Without one, the built-in permissions decide. `ALLOW` or `DENY` settle it; `DEFAULT` leaves it to the
permissions. As Java's EgradxFileAccessPolicy.

### EgradxFileScanner

Looks at an uploaded file before it is kept: a virus scanner, a content check. Called after the bytes are stored and
before the file's row is committed; a refusal deletes the bytes and answers FILE_REJECTED (422). As Java's EgradxFileScanner.

#### Methods

##### scan()

```ts
scan(upload): 
  | string
  | Promise<string | null | undefined>
  | null
  | undefined;
```

Why the file is refused, or undefined to keep it. `upload.open()` gives the stored bytes from the start, each time.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `upload` | \{ `contentType`: `string`; `name`: `string`; `organizationId`: `string`; `size`: `number`; `open`: `Promise`\<`Readable`\>; \} |
| `upload.contentType` | `string` |
| `upload.name` | `string` |
| `upload.organizationId` | `string` |
| `upload.size` | `number` |
| `upload.open` |

###### Returns

  \| `string`
  \| `Promise`\<`string` \| `null` \| `undefined`\>
  \| `null`
  \| `undefined`

### FileStorage

File storage as `@babulvaibhav/egradx-sdk` takes it (`createEgradx({ …, files: createFileStorage({ … }) })`): the SDK
connects it to egradx-auth before auth starts, starts and closes it with the rest, and egradxRoutes mounts its endpoints.

#### Properties

| Property | Modifier | Type | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
| <a id="property-files"></a> `files` | `readonly` | [`Files`](#files) | The library, once connected. |

##### close()

```ts
close(): Promise<void>;
```

###### Returns

`Promise`\<`void`\>

##### connect()

```ts
connect(libraries): void;
```

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `libraries` | \{ `auth`: `Pick`\<[`Auth`](/docs/reference/node/egradx-sdk#auth), `"contribute"` \| `"profiles"`\>; `log?`: [`FilesLog`](#fileslog); `observations?`: [`EgradxObservations`](/docs/reference/node/egradx-sdk#egradxobservations); `prisma`: [`PrismaLike`](/docs/reference/node/egradx-sdk#prismalike); \} |
| `libraries.auth` | `Pick`\<[`Auth`](/docs/reference/node/egradx-sdk#auth), `"contribute"` \| `"profiles"`\> |
| `libraries.log?` | [`FilesLog`](#fileslog) |
| `libraries.observations?` | [`EgradxObservations`](/docs/reference/node/egradx-sdk#egradxobservations) |
| `libraries.prisma` | [`PrismaLike`](/docs/reference/node/egradx-sdk#prismalike) |

`void`

### createFiles()

```ts
function createFiles(options): Files;
```

egradx-file-storage for Node, on the application's PrismaClient: the counterpart of Java's auto-configuration. Mount the
endpoints with `fileRoutes(files)` from `@babulvaibhav/egradx-file-storage/express`, and migrate with `migrateFiles`.

  await migrateFiles(databaseUrl);
  const files = createFiles({ prisma, auth, local: { root: './files' } });   // before auth.start()
  app.use(fileRoutes(files));
  await files.start();

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`FilesOptions`](#filesoptions) |
